text: Liver Fluke (Fasciola Hepatica) is picked up by grazing, requiring a small snail host to complete its cycle, so wet grazing areas carry the highest risk. Disease can be acute, sub-acute, or chronic — symptoms depend on fluke numbers and come from bleeding/tissue damage as immature flukes migrate through the liver, plus bile duct blockage and blood loss from adult flukes. Signs: loss of appetite, weight loss/emaciation, anemia (mucous membranes turn white instead of pink), chronic diarrhea, and jaw swelling. Treatment: Dovenix or Albendazole, with two treatments per year often needed. Intestinal worms: picked up grazing on larvae-contaminated pasture (adult worms in cattle shed eggs in manure, which hatch and develop into larvae on the grass). Signs: weight loss, reduced appetite without fever, green profuse diarrhea, rough coat. Treatment: Levamisole, Albendazole, or Ivermectin 1% (1 cc/50 kg, subcutaneous).
